title: 1 Corinthians Bible Quiz - Chapter 9
description: Ten questions on 1 Corinthians 9: the seal of an apostleship, the ox and the grain, the Good News without charge, and running to win the prize.

questions.text: What does verse 2 call the readers?
questions.explanation: The verse says they are the seal of his apostleship in the Lord.

answers.text: The crown of all his labor among the Gentiles
The first fruits of all who have believed
The seal of his apostleship in the Lord
His own letter written to the whole world

questions.text: Who is named in verse 5 along with the rest of the apostles and the brothers of the Lord?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 asks about the right to take along a believing wife, as the rest of the apostles do, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas.

answers.text: Cephas
Timothy
Apollos
Moses

questions.text: Which three examples does verse 7 use?
questions.explanation: The verse asks about a soldier who serves at his own expense, one who plants a vineyard, and one who feeds a flock.

answers.text: A farmer, a fisherman and a builder of houses
A runner, a wrestler and a man who boxes
A priest, a scribe and a judge of the people
A soldier, one who plants a vineyard and one who feeds a flock

questions.text: What is quoted from the law of Moses in verse 9?
questions.explanation: The verse quotes, "You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain."

answers.text: "You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together."
"You shall not muzzle an ox while it treads out the grain."
"The laborer is worthy of his food."
"You shall not glean your field twice."

questions.text: Why does verse 12 say they did not use this right?
questions.explanation: The verse says they bear all things so that they may cause no hindrance to the Good News of Christ.

answers.text: So that they would cause no hindrance to the Good News of Christ
Because the law of Moses did not allow them to
Because the assembly they wrote to was poor
Because the other apostles had forbidden it to them

questions.text: What did the Lord ordain, according to verse 14?
questions.explanation: The verse says the Lord ordained that those who proclaim the Good News should live from the Good News.

answers.text: That the apostles should work with their own hands
That the assemblies should send gifts to Jerusalem
That those who proclaim the Good News should live from the Good News
That teachers should take no wife

questions.text: What does the writer say his reward is, in verse 18?
questions.explanation: He says his reward is that when he preaches the Good News, he may present it without charge.

answers.text: To be counted among the apostles
To present the Good News without charge
To receive a crown from the assembly
To be sent to the Jews first

questions.text: Why does he say he has become all things to all men?
questions.explanation: Verse 22 says it is so that he may by all means save some.

answers.text: So that no one may accuse him
So that he may please the assembly
So that he may travel freely
So that he may by all means save some

questions.text: According to verse 25, what kind of crown do those who strive in the games receive?
questions.explanation: The verse says they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible one.

answers.text: An incorruptible crown
A crown of gold
A corruptible crown
No crown at all

questions.text: What does the writer say he does to his body in verse 27?
questions.explanation: The verse says he beats his body and brings it into submission, lest after preaching to others he himself should be rejected.

answers.text: He beats it and brings it into submission
He feeds it well for the race
He leaves it to the Lord
He covers it with sackcloth
